title: Remeasured: the population lost its best genome; flights 32 -> 64
text: Champions re-flown on the same 1,000 analysis seeds (C++ sim, real task): gen 432 54.4%, 682 65.4%, 1432 78.2%, 1932 81.9%, 2432 85.0%, 2462 (the 90% check) 88.1%, 2932 86.5%, 3182 80.7%, 3352 83.4%, 3402 83.0%. Variance halves (standard error ~4.5 points); generations take ~2x longer (~9,000 left before Friday instead of ~17,000). text: Diagnosis (200 analysis flights each): the gen-211 champion landed 97.5% in its current training world, 67% in full wind without a boulder (gen 100: 15.5%), 0% in calm air with a boulder (73% boulder hits), 1% on the real task. Changes at gen 230: (1) ramps are paced: 3 steps per generation while the champion lands >= 90% of its own flights in the current world, 1 at >= 70%, 0.5 below; (2) the stage's final world is checked every 10 generations from the start and passing it (plus confirmation) ends the stage at once, even mid-ramp; (3) 25% of stage-2 flights carry a 40%-size boulder (not counted for pace or pass) so route learning starts early; (4) at the deadline (minus 20 min) the trainer stops, re-flies the 5 best-checked champions plus the newest on 1,000 fresh selection flights and picks one; the supervisor then flies both test blocks automatically, also after a goal stop; (5) the local dashboard shows the newest champion flying in its current world. First check after the change: real task 15.5% (new best), stage final world 61%.

title: Crash after the species fix; threshold set by measurement
text: After the resume fix, the threshold I restarted with (0.3) split the population into 105 species, and neat-python stopped with an error (105 species x 3 genomes minimum > 300 genomes). The supervisor restarted it twice from the gen-196 checkpoint with the same result; no generations were lost beyond these retries. This time I chose the threshold by simulation on the saved population: 0.3 -> 79 species, 0.4 -> 13, 0.45 -> 6, 0.5 and above -> 3. Set to 0.4. Guard added so this cannot stop the run again: when there are very many species, the per-species minimum and elitism shrink for that generation and the threshold rises 30% per generation instead of 5%.

title: Correction: species collapsed because of a resume bug, not the threshold floor
text: At the 16:45 check-in I blamed the species collapse (13 -> 3) on the threshold floor of 0.15 and lowered it to 0.05. That was wrong: species stayed at 3. Measured on the gen-195 checkpoint: members sit 0.37-0.48 from their representative, which is impossible with a threshold of 0.05. Cause: when the run resumes, the species set comes back from the pickle with its own copy of the settings, so speciation kept the threshold it had at the first restart (gen 57): 46.8, the runaway value. Since gen 57 every genome was lumped into an existing species and stagnation removed them down to the 3 protected by species_elitism; my controller was tuning a number nobody read. Fix: on resume, the species set and the trainer share one settings object, and a test checks it. Expectation before the result: new species form within a few generations (threshold restarts at 0.3), heading for ~12.

title: Bug found: the species threshold ran away (0.25 -> 35)
text: Check-in at gen 54. Calm landing is learned: the champion lands 100% of its calm training flights since gen 18 (training wheels still 0.82 -> 0.46), mean fitness -342 -> +179. But my speciation controller is broken: it raises the compatibility threshold 10% per generation whenever there are more than 12 species, and the count has been stuck at 14 since gen 3 while the threshold went 0.25 -> 35. neat-python keeps old species as long as genomes stay within the threshold of their representative, so the count never responded. With a threshold of 35 no new species can form; as stagnant species are removed, the population would collapse into one species and new structure would lose its protection. Change (one): clamp the threshold to 0.15-1.0 and step it 5% per generation; reset it to 0.5 at the restart. Expectation before the result: the species count should drift towards ~12, and calm-landing progress should not suffer.

title: Run N1 starts: NEAT from random genomes, goal 95%
text: The user's decision today: NEAT from scratch with a curriculum, a population big enough to evolve, nodes that can be added and removed; stop at 95% or Friday 17:00 (the brief's 98% is lowered to 95%). Set-up: population 300, every genome 16 inputs -> 32 random tanh hidden nodes -> 4 outputs (640 connections), weights random; mutation nudges 80% of weights by N(0, 0.1), adds nodes (3%) and connections (5%), deletes nodes (2%) and connections (2%). Speciation retuned every generation to keep ~12 species. All genomes of a generation fly the same seeds; the top 10 re-fly 40 selection seeds. Curriculum N1: calm landing with fading training wheels -> wind ramp 5->15 with turbulence -> boulder growing 0.4->1.0 with 40% real-task rehearsal -> real task with 30% hard cases. Speed in the Python reference simulator: ~40,000-50,000 steps/s on 7 workers, ~20 s per calm generation; the C++ simulator is postponed until speed is the bottleneck. Expectation written before the result: >= 90% calm landings within ~250 generations.

title: Boulder layout v3 in the frozen task
text: One approved change to the world: the boulder's bottom now stays at least 3.5 m above the pad (v2: 1.73 m, less than the lander's 1.8 m height). Same random stream as v2, so each seed keeps its boulder size and sideways position; only the height moved, into a 3.0 m band.
